resources.string: Optional fallback that filters selected key events while Android delivers them to Accessibility. It does not inspect screen contents or typed text.
Silence headset controls. Keep the phone buttons yours.
Media and the selected headset’s volume buttons are guarded with the screen on or off.
Media buttons are guarded. Select the headset input device to guard its volume buttons too.
A requested route is not active yet. Automatic recovery is armed; reconnect Shizuku or rescan only if it stays here.
No privileged headset buttons are being blocked.
Start Shizuku. Button Silencer will reconnect when its binder returns.
Grant Button Silencer permission from the Shizuku prompt or app.
The screen-off protection service is being attached.
Connect the USB DAC / IEM, then scan for its volume-key input node.
Only the chosen external input node is monitored. The phone’s built-in side buttons remain outside this route.
Media blocking is enabled. Scan and select the headset to block its volume buttons too.
Select the headset input device first.
No external volume-key input was found. Connect the headset, keep Shizuku running, and scan again.
Only devices that look like the phone’s own buttons were found, so none were offered.
Neutralize volume buttons from selected headset

The media listener consumes media keys before normal media sessions. The volume route watches only the selected input node and restores media volume after its volume presses. Recovery is event-driven with bounded retries; there is no wake lock or permanent polling loop.
Block volume keys from every device
Caution: the last option can also disable the phone’s own volume buttons while Accessibility receives them.
Off by default for minimum overhead. When enabled, recognized events are kept only in memory for this app session and are never sent anywhere.
No recognized Accessibility events in this session.
A compact Android utility for suppressing unwanted headset controls while keeping the phone’s physical buttons usable.
No network permission, analytics, ads, account, USB interface claim, continuous polling loop, or persistent event history.
Shizuku must be running after a reboot. Release builds are minified and resource-shrunk.
